profile.reading:
This building is identified in mapping data as an Amazon Web Services facility near Micron Drive in San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas. DataCenterDynamics reported that AWS had filed plans to develop data centers in the San Antonio area, and the San Antonio Report has described Bexar County as home to at least 30 data centers from multiple operators as of 2026, citing membership of Amazon, Microsoft, and Google in the Data Center Coalition industry group active in the region. Local and trade press separately reported that Amazon Data Services Inc. filed Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation permits in March 2026 for three San Antonio-area data center projects, at 2200 Texas 211 (roughly $65 million, 109,000 square feet), on the West Side (141,979 square feet), and on the Southeast Side (119,407 square feet). This research could not confirm with confidence whether any of those three specific filings corresponds to this exact registry entry near Micron Drive, as opposed to a separate nearby Amazon project in the same metro area.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating that this research could confirm applies specifically to this mapped location, and no source found for this page breaks the San Antonio-area AWS footprint down building by building with certainty at this coordinate.

Amazon is widely reported in trade and business press to acquire and hold United States data center real estate through a subsidiary named Vadata, Inc., rather than directly under the Amazon.com or AWS names, a practice also seen with AWS campuses in Virginia, Ohio, Oregon, and elsewhere. This research did not pull a Bexar County Appraisal District or Tarrant Appraisal District parcel record to confirm Vadata, or another Amazon-linked entity, as the owner of the specific parcel at this coordinate; that county-level confirmation step, which the assignment for this page identifies as the most reliable source for hyperscaler-owned parcels with no public announcement, was not completed this pass and is noted here as follow-up work rather than assumed.

profile.regional_context: San Antonio and Bexar County, Texas have become an active data center market, with the San Antonio Report citing at least 30 facilities from multiple operators as of 2026, including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, CyrusOne, and Vantage Data Centers. CPS Energy, the city-owned utility, supplies power locally, and Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have negotiated economic development incentive agreements with several data center developers as the sector has grown, a trend covered by the San Antonio Report and regional business press. Texas as a whole has drawn large hyperscale data center investment in recent years, including AWS filings for other campuses near Houston, reported by DataCenterDynamics.

reading.body:
AWS does not publish specific power capacity, square footage, or technical specifications for individual data centers, citing security and operational policy. This facility in Bexar County is confirmed to exist at the stated address on Micron Drive in San Antonio, but no published capacity figure is available to assess its scale or role in AI workload hosting.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only 18 publish power capacity figures totaling 468 megawatts. This campus cannot be ranked among the published capacity in Texas because AWS does not disclose its specifications, placing it outside the 18 facilities with public MW data.

Without published specifications, this facility's relevance to AI scaling cannot be determined from operator disclosures. The absence of a capacity figure is a policy choice by AWS rather than evidence the facility is inactive, but it means this campus contributes no quantifiable data to assessments of Texas grid constraints on AI compute growth.
